title: Design gate consumes Dispatch document approval (artifact.approved) instead of an Approve ask
branch: legion/LEGION-20 on sjawhar/legion. Rebased three times: onto main 7add4d03 at phase start; onto main fd4fce51 (v1.11.1) after GitHub reported #975 CONFLICTING (#971 conflicts, see decisionsTaken); and onto main 4d516a1f (pi-envoy v1.17.2) on 2026-09-13 ~01:45Z after GitHub reported CONFLICTING again — #962 (runtime boundary, LEGION-21) had taken state version 24 for its locator migration, so this branch's gate migration is now v24 -> v25 (migrateV24State, chained after main's migrateV23State); processes.ts's fragment call moved to the new issueInnerCommand shape; processes.test.ts keeps both sides' helpers.
summary: The Legion daemon's design gate is now a human's approval of the root issue's spec document, pinned to a document version, instead of an answered Approve question. The gate record is { artifactId, latestVersion, approvedVersion? } (state version 24), open exactly when approvedVersion equals latestVersion (designGateOpen). Three Dispatch issue events drive it: artifact.approved records the version and wakes the architect with the unchanged design-approved payload only when the gate is then open; artifact.changes_requested retracts the approval and wakes design-changes-requested with the reviewer's reason; artifact.version raises the latest version silently, so an edited spec is closed until re-approved. ask.answered no longer touches the gate. register_gate takes { issue, artifactId, version } from dispatch_request_approval's result and rejects the retired askId field with a 400 naming the field. Existing v23 state migrates once at boot by reading each kept gate's spec document from Dispatch; closed or tree-less gates are dropped with a log line and a failed read refuses startup naming the issue. The root architect's system prompt states the project's gate policy in one sentence; skills, role prompts, AGENTS documentation, and the smoke rig's checkpoints 3 and 4 follow. No legion approve command or approve route was built (plan decision D1). No plan document was added to the repository.

decisionsTaken.topic: gates.design: off keeps today's semantics in the new gate shape
decisionsTaken.detail: The plan did not name the daemon's existing gate-off path (the GATE_OFF_APPROVAL marker in handleGatesRegister and the boot fixup in index.ts), whose fields vanished with the record shape. Deleting it or keeping it were both possible; I kept it in the new shape: under `off`, register_gate records the gate approved at the registered version (approvedVersion = latestVersion) and publishes design-approved, and boot approves every registered-but-closed gate of an active tree the same way. Reasoning: the spec names `gates.design: off` as the operator's only bypass and this is its mechanical form, so an architect that registers a gate anyway under `off` proceeds instead of parking forever; a well-behaved architect never reaches it because the prompt fragment (D4) tells it not to register. The GATE_OFF_APPROVAL string constant is gone since the record has no marker field; a gate-off approval is indistinguishable in state from a human approval at that version. Reversing this is a small change in api/routes/issues.ts and index.ts plus two tests (api.test.ts 'with gates.design off ...', index.test.ts 'with gates.design off, boot approves ...'). Sent to the architect topic before this handoff; the role had no live holder (404), so this record is the notice.

decisionsTaken.detail: #971 (merged after the plan) taught the daemon to close the architect's gate-off ask on Dispatch (DispatchClient.resolveAsk, GATE_OFF_ASK_REASON, satisfyGateOff) and rewrote the smoke rig around it. On this branch the daemon opens and tracks no ask — register_gate carries a document id and version, and under gates.design: off the architect is told to request nothing — so there is nothing for the daemon to close. Resolution: api/routes/issues.ts, api.test.ts, and the four docs keep this branch's text; index.ts and index.test.ts keep #966/#967's other edits and this branch's gate-off fixup (approve at latestVersion, wake; no ask). Residual edge, not addressed: a gate registered under root-issues whose operator later flips to off leaves the approval request open on Dispatch, since the daemon does not know that ask's id; a human can resolve it from the dashboard.

decisionsTaken.topic: Smoke rig design-gate mode: keep main's default `off`, make `root-issues` selectable (SMOKE_DESIGN_GATE)
decisionsTaken.detail: #971 also switched scripts/smoke/up.sh to gates.design: off ('a smoke exercise must run end to end with nobody answering a design-gate ask') and made checkpoint 3 assert the gate-off path, while plan step 10 and spec acceptance 7 assume root-issues (a human approves the document between checkpoints 3 and 4). Under this branch's off semantics a compliant architect registers no gate, so the plan's checkpoint 3 could never pass against main's rig. Resolution, mirroring the rig's existing recorded webhook-mode pattern: up.sh takes SMOKE_DESIGN_GATE (off, the default, matching main; or root-issues), writes it into legion.yaml, and records it at ${SMOKE_DIR}/design-gate; checkpoints 3 and 4 read the record. Under off, checkpoint 3 proves the architect obeyed its policy line (spec posted, no gate registered, no approval request open, child exists) and checkpoint 4 checks the release alone; under root-issues both carry the plan's assertions (gate at the spec's current version with approval.state awaiting; approvedVersion == latestVersion recorded). Acceptance 7's human-approval proof therefore runs with SMOKE_DESIGN_GATE=root-issues on a scratch Dispatch server. Architect may veto: reverting to a fixed root-issues rig is a one-line change in up.sh plus dropping the off branch of the checkpoints.

decisionsTaken.topic: Architect ruling (review round 1, blocking): register_gate reads the document's approval from Dispatch
decisionsTaken.detail: Reviewer thread https://github.com/sjawhar/legion/pull/975#discussion_r3998678359: a human approval landing before register_gate was lost (reducer ignores artifact.approved for an unregistered document; Dispatch never re-emits it; dispatch_request_approval on an approved document returns ask null) and the architect parked forever. Ruling (architect, matching the reviewer): in handleGatesRegister, when the resulting gate would not be open and gates.design is not off, read the issue once via ctx.deps.dispatchClient.getIssue (the specArtifactResolver read), find the registered artifactId in artifacts, and seed from its approval — approved with version === latest_version: approvedVersion = version and publish design-approved through publishDesignApproved (the gates.design off path); stale: approvedVersion = version, closed, no wake; any other state: no approvedVersion. Dispatch's latest_version raises latestVersion in every seeded case (Dispatch is authoritative on the current version). The read happens before recording; a failed read records nothing and returns 502 so register_gate retries. Implementer's addition within the ruling: a registered document the issue does not carry is a 404 naming both (a gate for it could never open; crash loud, no silent record). Humans still write every approval; the daemon only reads. gates.design: off does not read Dispatch (the daemon approves itself). Tests: approved-at-latest → open + one wake, re-registration reads nothing; stale → closed, latestVersion raised, no wake; awaiting → unapproved, one read per closed registration; read failure → 502 no gate; unknown document → 404. AGENTS.md (daemon: /gates/register row, design-gate bullet, 'only Dispatch read outside resync' sentence now names both reads; root: gate paragraph), dispatch-client.ts comment, and the architect skill (already-approved result still registers) updated. .legion/plan.json left as history per the architect.

decisionsTaken.topic: Architect ruling (tester round 3, acceptance 6): one --append-system-prompt per pane — Oh My Pi's flag is last-wins
decisionsTaken.detail: Tester finding on the real surface: on both Oh My Pi fork pins — 18.1.18-sami.20260912-203541 (production panes) and the repository pin 18.1.18-sami.20260912-104423 — the binary's argv handler is `"--append-system-prompt": (e, s) => { e.appendSystemPrompt = s; }` (last-wins). The daemon passed several flags per pane (role prompt from roles/*.md; the addressing line, which on this branch carries the design-gate policy; since #956 the deployment `instructions:` text), so only the last reached the model; with `instructions:` configured — production LEGION has it — a pane got only the deployment instructions, and a real armed-gate architect on this head's rig skipped the gate ('the gate policy line isn't visible at the end of my system prompt'). Ruling: systemPromptArguments emits exactly ONE `--append-system-prompt` whose value is every fragment joined in the existing order — role prompt, addressing (+ gate policy for the root), deployment instructions — separated by a blank line; no fragment dropped, no reordering, nothing else in the argv changes; holds on any OMP build. Implementation: one double-quoted shell word — the file-backed parts stay `$(cat <path>)` (expanded by the pane's shell), the addressing text is escaped for double quotes (`\`, `"`, `$`, backtick), the blank lines are literal newlines inside the word (dash and bash both accept them; proven with a recorder under /bin/sh=dash and /bin/bash). Tests per the ruling: processes.test.ts argv pins go through one promptArgument helper; main's #956 deployment-instructions test asserts exactly one flag for root (gate policy + instructions), worker, and controller plus the part order inside the root's value; root without instructions, resumed root, gate-off root, and the tester worker pins cover the rest; index.test.ts controller pin; the real-tmux e2e (real shell → argv recorder) expects one flag holding the role prompt, a blank line, then the materialized instructions. Direct check with `omp -p` (--model claude-haiku-4-5, throwaway OMP profile, pane vars scrubbed) on BOTH pins: one joined flag of three marked parts → reply 'ALPHA-ROLE, BRAVO-ADDRESSING, CHARLIE-INSTRUCTIONS'; control with three flags on the repository pin → reply 'CHARLIE-INSTRUCTIONS' only. Wording updated: daemon AGENTS.md (instructions paragraph and the design-gate bullet's 'second --append-system-prompt fragment'), processes.ts deps comment, config.ts, deployment-instructions.ts, pi-envoy AGENTS.md, the processes test name; root AGENTS.md already said 'in its system prompt'. PR body: architect paragraph ('Its system prompt states whether…'), processes.ts Files line, a verification sentence crediting the tester's real-surface find.

pullRequest.title: feat(daemon): the design gate is a human approving the spec document, not an answered Approve question (LEGION-20)
pullRequest.body:
When a Legion project has its design gate turned on, the architect used to post a yes/no question ("Approve?") on the root issue and the Legion daemon waited for a human to answer it. With this change the daemon waits instead for a human to approve the root issue's spec document itself, at a specific version, the way a pull-request review is pinned to a commit; if the spec is edited after approval, the gate closes again until someone approves the new version. We know it works because reducer tests fed the exact approval, changes-requested, and new-version events the Dispatch server publishes open, close, and reopen the gate as described; the daemon's saved state from the current release upgrades without losing any gate; and the smoke rig's design-gate checkpoints now pass by approving the document rather than answering a question.

Dispatch: LEGION-20

This implements LEGION-20, "Design gate consumes Dispatch document approval (artifact.approved) instead of an Approve ask". It builds on pull request #946, "feat(dispatch): a spec can be approved - a human review pinned to a document version", which added the Dispatch server side (the review record, the `approval` field on every document read, the `artifact.approved` and `artifact.changes_requested` events, and the `dispatch_request_approval` tool) and is already on main.

## What changed, for whom

**For a human approving a spec.** Approve the document from its header on the Dispatch dashboard, or answer the approval question in the Inbox. Nothing else to click, and timing does not matter: an approval given before the architect has finished registering the gate is picked up when it registers. Requesting changes (with a reason) closes the gate and tells the architect why. Editing the spec after approval closes the gate until you approve the new version.

**For the root architect (an agent).** Its system prompt states whether this project arms the design gate (`gates.design: root-issues`) or not (`gates.design: off`) — in the addressing part, after the role prompt; deployment instructions, when configured, follow it. When armed, it writes the spec, calls `dispatch_request_approval` on it, registers the returned document id and version with the daemon, and parks until the `design-approved` wake — which arrives at once if a human already approved that version. When off, it writes the spec and continues with no approval step at all. Previously the daemon reported the policy only to the extension, never to the model, which is how architects opened approval questions in a project with the gate off.

**For an operator.** There is no operator command to open a gate and no agent path either; a project that does not want the gate runs `gates.design: off` in its `legion.yaml`. The daemon's saved state upgrades itself on the first start after this change (state version 25 to 26 — pull request #993, "feat(daemon): handoff-only pushes are not fix attempts; pr-blocked once per count (LEGION-33)", took version 25 on main while this branch was in review, so the gate migration moved up one) by reading each open gate's spec document from Dispatch once; a gate whose tree is already closed is dropped with a log line naming the issue, and if Dispatch cannot be reached for a gate that is still open, the daemon refuses to start and names the issue rather than guessing. The installed `@sjawhar/pi-legion-envoy` plugin must be the release built from this change: the daemon now requires daemon API contract 2 and refuses to start with an older plugin, naming both versions.

## Files, and what each is for

- `packages/daemon/src/daemon/legion-state.ts` (the daemon's durable state and its upgrade migrations): the gate record becomes `{ artifactId, latestVersion, approvedVersion? }`, with `designGateOpen` as the one place that decides whether it is open; the state version 25 to 26 migration described above, written to disk as soon as it runs so a restart never repeats its Dispatch reads.
- `packages/daemon/src/daemon/dispatch-client.ts` (the daemon's HTTP client for Dispatch): `specArtifactResolver`, the read the migration uses (an issue's primary document id and its highest version number). The method pull request #971 ("fix(daemon): a gate-off design ask is closed on Dispatch, never left in a human's inbox") added for closing the gate question is removed; nothing opens a question any more.
- `packages/daemon/src/daemon/dispatch-events.ts` (decodes Dispatch events before any state change): a review or version event missing the fields the gate needs is rejected as a malformed event, logged and dropped, never fed to state.
- `packages/daemon/src/daemon/reducers.ts` (turns Dispatch events into state changes and wakes): the three document events drive the gate; an answered question no longer does.
- `packages/daemon/src/daemon/api/routes/issues.ts`, `api/http.ts`, `api/state.ts` (the daemon's local HTTP API): `register_gate` takes the document id (stored lowercase, as Dispatch writes it) and version; a request naming the old `askId` field, or missing a field, is rejected with a message naming the field; the state read-out shows the new record. When the gate would be closed after registering, the daemon reads the document's approval from Dispatch once first: a human who approved before the architect registered (from the document header, or from the Inbox between the request and the registration) opens the gate right there, with the same wake an approval event produces; an approval of an older version is recorded but leaves the gate closed. The daemon never writes an approval — it copies one a human already gave. If Dispatch cannot be read, the registration fails and the architect retries it.
- `packages/daemon/src/daemon/catchup.ts` (the snapshot handed to an architect that reconnects): each gate is reported with an `open` flag so the architect never re-derives it.
- `packages/daemon/src/daemon/processes.ts` (builds every pane's launch command): one sentence stating the gate policy is added to the root architect's system prompt. Every pane's system-prompt parts — the role prompt, the addressing line (with that sentence for the root), and the deployment instructions when configured — are now handed to Oh My Pi as a single `--append-system-prompt` argument, joined by blank lines. Oh My Pi's flag keeps only the last value it is given, on both the production build (`18.1.18-sami.20260912-203541`) and the repository pin (`18.1.18-sami.20260912-104423`), so the separate flags used until now left a pane with only its last fragment: with deployment instructions configured, no role prompt, no addressing, and no gate policy. Found by the tester on the real surface, where an armed-gate architect skipped the gate for exactly that reason.
- `packages/contracts/src/legion-daemon-api.ts` (the shared request and response shapes between the daemon and the extension): the gate shape and the `register_gate` request; the document id must be a UUID, so a slug or file name is refused with a message naming the field.
- `packages/envoy-client/src/dispatch-execute.ts` (runs the Dispatch tools for agents): `dispatch_request_approval`'s result now states the document id, the value the architect must copy into `register_gate` — in both the "approval requested" and the "already approved" answers.
- `packages/pi-envoy/src/legion/tools.ts` (the `legion` tool agents call): `register_gate` takes `artifactId` and `version`, checking the id against the shared contract's own definition before the round trip.
- `skills/legion-architect/SKILL.md`, `skills/legion-controller/SKILL.md`, `packages/pi-envoy/roles/architect-root.md`, `packages/pi-envoy/roles/architect.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `packages/daemon/src/daemon/AGENTS.md` (the instructions agents and people read): describe the gate as document approval.
- `scripts/smoke/up.sh`, `scripts/smoke/checkpoints.sh`, `scripts/smoke/checkpoints.test.sh`, `scripts/smoke/README.md` (the end-to-end smoke rig): the rig creates its root issue with `force` so a rerun against a used project no longer trips Dispatch's duplicate detector, and `SMOKE_OMP_PIN` lets it run the OMP build production is pinned to; the rig's design-gate policy comes from `SMOKE_DESIGN_GATE` and is recorded beside the rig's config. With the default `off` (what main already runs, so a smoke exercise stays unattended) checkpoint 3 checks that the architect registered no gate and left no approval request open; with `root-issues` checkpoint 3 checks that the spec document has an open approval request and checkpoint 4 that the daemon recorded the human's approval. With the gate armed, checkpoint 3 proves the architect asked and waited — the approval request is open and nothing has moved past the gate (no child released, no phase worker claimed; a child sitting in triage or backlog is fine) — and checkpoint 4 proves the approval opened the gate and the tree then moved, by a released child or a phase worker on the root itself (a single-issue tree), naming which it saw; with the gate off, checkpoint 3 checks that same movement directly.
- Test fixtures under `packages/daemon/src/daemon/__tests__/fixtures/dispatch/`: three new event fixtures built from the published contract; the two old question fixtures that nothing used anymore are deleted.

## Verification
